article.title: Iran steps up pressure on Kurdish opposition in Iraq
paras: Editor's note: this story was translated from the original VOA Kurdi article.
With a lull in the U.S. Iran conflict and the September completion of the withdrawal of American forces from Iraq, Iran appears to be increasing pressure on Iranian Kurdish opposition groups.

The actions against Kurdish groups based in Iraq's autonomous Kurdistan Region are a test of Baghdad's independence and analysts are warning Tehran retains considerable influence over Iraqi political decisions.

Iranian news agencies reported that Iraqi and Iranian officials agreed during talks on Monday to relocate members of Iranian Kurdish opposition groups from the Kurdistan Region. Iranian Ambassador to Iraq Mohammad Kazem al-Sadegh said Tuesday that both countries had agreed to expel groups Tehran describes as separatist terrorists or hand their members over to Iran.
Iraqi officials confirmed the meeting, attended by representatives of the Kurdistan Regional Government, but made no mention of an agreement to expel or extradite opposition members.
Iraq's National Security Advisory Agency said the discussions, chaired by National Security Advisor Qassim Aboudi, focused on resolving outstanding issues under a bilateral security agreement.
The conflicting accounts highlight the political sensitivities surrounding Iranian Kurdish groups, which have maintained bases in northern Iraq for decades.
Hazhar Barnji, U.S. representative of the Kurdistan Democratic Party of Iran (KDPI), told VOA that the party had received no official notification of any relocation decision.
"To date, we have not received such official communication or indication from either the Iraqi federal government or the Kurdistan Regional Government," Barnji said.
He said the party respected Iraqi sovereignty and international law, while its principal political activities remained focused on Iranian Kurdistan.

Washington-based Iraqi political figure Entifadh Qanbar said Iran's influence over armed factions continued to constrain Baghdad's decision-making despite American efforts to weaken Tehran's regional reach.
"In reality, Iraq is currently governed by armed groups and the will of those forces," Qanbar told VOA, arguing that Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi had little ability to restrain them.
"Iraq will not emerge from Tehran's control unless a fundamental political change takes place," he said.

Political analyst Isam Fayli told VOA that Tehran's concerns extended beyond border security to fears that Kurdish opposition movements could gain broader support inside Iran and emerge as a more significant political challenge.

Fayli warned that Iraq handing opposition members to Iran could raise serious legal and humanitarian concerns. He suggested international assistance in finding safe resettlement arrangements, citing the relocation of members of the exiled Iranian opposition group Mujahedin-e Khalq.
Sheikh Ghaith al-Tamimi, head of the Iraqi Citizenship Project, said Iraq's own history demonstrated the limitations of military approaches to Kurdish political demands.

He said Baghdad's security cooperation with neighboring countries must respect constitutional and international obligations rather than become an instrument for settling another government's political disputes.

The changing U.S. military presence, Tamimi argued, presents a crucial test of whether Iraqi institutions can make independent security decisions or remain vulnerable to foreign influence and powerful armed factions.

For Iranian Kurdish opposition groups, the immediate question is whether Tehran's reported agreement with Baghdad will translate into concrete action, given that previous agreements between the two governments have failed to result in the expulsion of these groups from Iraqi Kurdistan.
zh: 伊朗加強對伊拉克庫德族反對派的施壓
編者註：本文翻譯自美國之音（VOA）庫爾德語版原文。
隨著美伊衝突趨於平息，加上美軍已於九月完成從伊拉克撤軍，伊朗似乎正加強對伊朗庫德族反對派團體的施壓。
針對駐紮於伊拉克庫德自治區的庫德族團體所採取的行動，是對巴格達獨立性的考驗；分析人士警告，德黑蘭對伊拉克的政治決策仍保有相當大的影響力。
伊朗新聞機構報導，伊拉克與伊朗官員週一在會談中達成共識，將把伊朗庫德族反對派團體的成員從庫德斯坦地區遷出。伊朗駐伊拉克大使穆罕默德·卡齊姆·薩迪格週二表示，兩國已同意驅逐德黑蘭方面所稱的「分裂主義恐怖組織」，或將其成員移交伊朗。
伊拉克官員證實了此次會議，庫德斯坦區域政府的代表出席了會議，但並未提及任何關於驅逐或引渡反對派成員的協議。
伊拉克國家安全諮詢局表示，這場由國家安全顧問卡西姆·阿布迪主持的會談，重點在於解決雙邊安全協定下的未決問題。
這些相互矛盾的說法凸顯了圍繞伊朗庫德族團體的政治敏感性，這些團體數十年來一直在伊拉克北部維持據點。
伊朗庫德民主黨（KDPI）駐美代表哈扎爾·巴恩吉向美國之音表示，該黨尚未收到任何關於搬遷決定的官方通知。
「迄今為止，我們尚未收到來自伊拉克聯邦政府或庫德斯坦地區政府的任何此類官方通告或跡象，」巴恩吉表示。
他表示，該黨尊重伊拉克的主權和國際法，但其主要政治活動仍以伊朗庫爾德斯坦為重點。
駐華盛頓的伊拉克政治人物恩蒂法德·坎巴爾表示，儘管美國致力於削弱德黑蘭在該地區的影響力，但伊朗對武裝派系的影響力仍持續限制著巴格達的決策空間。
「事實上，伊拉克目前是由武裝團體及其意志所統治的，」坎巴爾對美國之音表示，並指出伊拉克總理阿里·扎伊迪幾乎無力約束這些勢力。
「除非發生根本性的政治變革，否則伊拉克將無法擺脫德黑蘭的控制，」他說道。
政治分析師伊薩姆·法伊利向美國之音表示，德黑蘭的擔憂不僅限於邊境安全，更擔心庫德族反對運動可能在伊朗國內獲得更廣泛的支持，並演變成更重大的政治挑戰。
法伊利警告稱，伊拉克若將反對派成員移交伊朗，可能會引發嚴重的法律及人道主義疑慮。他建議國際社會提供協助，為這些人尋求安全的安置方案，並以流亡的伊朗反對派組織「人民聖戰者組織」成員的安置案例為例。
「伊拉克公民權計畫」負責人謝赫·蓋斯·塔米米表示，伊拉克自身的歷史已證明，以軍事手段應對庫德族的政治訴求存在局限性。
他表示，巴格達與鄰國之間的安全合作必須遵守憲法及國際義務，而非淪為解決他國政府政治糾紛的工具。
塔米米指出，美國軍事存在態勢的變化，將成為一項關鍵考驗，檢驗伊拉克各機構究竟能否獨立做出安全決策，抑或仍會受制於外國影響及強大的武裝派系。
對伊朗庫德族反對派團體而言，當前的關鍵問題在於，鑑於兩國政府先前達成的協議均未能促使這些團體被驅逐出伊拉克庫德斯坦，據報德黑蘭與巴格達達成的這項協議是否會轉化為具體行動。
